deep.reconstruction:
PART A: A proof of Königsberger's irreducibility theorem.

The page cites 'S. 5 meines Separatabzuges Berl. Berichte Nov. 1894'. This is most likely L. Königsberger's 1894 Sitzungsberichte note on the irreducibility of algebraic equations. That note is not reproduced here, so its exact statement and the precise form of 'Gleichung (6)' are inferred from Hilbert's argument (my reconstruction).

Setting (inferred):
- f(x) = a_0 x^n + a_1 x^{n-1} + ... + a_n has rational integer coefficients, and n = mu*nu.
- Hilbert normalises a_0 = 1.
- The p-adic hypotheses (an Eisenstein-type, single-slope Newton polygon condition) make p^{-i/mu} a_i integral and leave a_n/p^{n/mu} = a_n/p^nu prime to p. Equivalently, v_p(a_i) >= i/mu and v_p(a_n) = nu.
- Analogous hypotheses hold for a second prime q with mu and nu interchanged: v_q(a_i) >= i/nu and v_q(a_n) = mu, with gcd(mu, nu) = 1.
- Claim: f is irreducible over Q.

Hilbert's proof:
1. Let alpha = alpha^(0), ..., alpha^(n-1) be the roots. Then beta = alpha/p^{1/mu} is a root of the monic polynomial p^{-n/mu} f(p^{1/mu} y). Its coefficients a_i p^{-i/mu} are algebraic integers, so beta is an algebraic integer.
2. The product of all the conjugates is prod alpha^(k)/p^{1/mu} = ± a_n/p^{n/mu}. This is an integer prime to p.
3. Each factor is an algebraic integer and the product is prime to p, so each factor, in particular alpha/p^{1/mu}, is prime to p. In valuation terms, every prime above p has w(alpha) = w(p)/mu.
4. In K = Q(alpha), of degree n', put j = (alpha, p), the ideal gcd. Then j^mu = (p).
   - Implicit step (mine): locally at each prime above p, (alpha, p) = (alpha) and (alpha)^mu = (p).
   - Away from p, (alpha, p) = 1.
5. Take norms from K, writing N(j) = p^f. Then p^{n'} = N((p)) = N(j)^mu = p^{f mu}, so mu divides n'.
6. The same argument with q and nu shows that nu divides n'.
   - Implicit step (mine): mu and nu are coprime, so mu*nu = n divides n'. Since n' <= n, we get n' = n, i.e. f is irreducible.
7. Remark on alternatives: the proof can also be run through Kronecker's Fundamentalgleichung (Kronecker, Grundzüge, pp. 111 and 115) and Hensel, Crelle 113, pp. 74-75.

PART B (begins at the bottom, continues on the next page): class number of a genus-0 function field.
- Claim: a field of algebraic functions of one variable of genus 0 has finite class number, equal to the degree n.
- The next page adds: the n-th power of every prime ideal is equivalent to 1.
- Modern reading: ideals of the field are taken relative to a plane model of degree n, with principal classes given by quotients of forms of equal degree. The ideal classes are then divisor classes modulo the hyperplane (line) section class.
- For genus 0, Pic(curve) ≅ Z via degree, and the hyperplane class has degree n. Hence the class group is Z/nZ, generated by any prime (point) divisor.
errors: The line 'Ebenso folgt die Theilbarkeit durch mu' should read 'durch nu'. The second application (to another prime with exponent 1/nu) yields nu | n'; together with mu | n' and gcd(mu, nu) = 1 this gives n' = mu*nu = n. As written ('durch mu' twice) the conclusion does not follow. This is a slip by Hilbert or a transcription misreading of nu.
The coprimality gcd(mu, nu) = 1 and the hypotheses for the second prime are not stated on the page; they must come from Königsberger's statement (equation (6)).
Step 3 ('the product is prime to p, hence each factor is prime to p') is correct but is stated without justification. It needs the integrality of every factor, which Hilbert did establish.
The definition of j is written ambiguously, possibly as (alpha, p^{1/mu}). The ideal must live in Q(alpha) for the norm argument to work, so (alpha, p) is the correct reading.

results.what: Irreducibility of an integer polynomial whose p-adic Newton polygon has a single slope 1/mu (and q-adic slope 1/nu, with gcd(mu, nu) = 1). Proved via the ideal factorisation (alpha, p)^mu = (p) and a norm/degree count.
results.modern_name: Generalized Eisenstein criterion / Newton polygon irreducibility criterion (Königsberger-Netto-Dumas); ramification index divides the field degree
results.usually_credited_to: Königsberger (1894), Netto (1895), Dumas (1906); Eisenstein/Schönemann for the basic case

results.what: Class number of a genus-0 algebraic function field (ideal classes modulo line sections of a degree-n model) equals n; the n-th power of each prime ideal is principal.
results.modern_name: Pic(P^1) ≅ Z, so divisor classes modulo the hyperplane class form Z/nZ
results.usually_credited_to: Implicit in Dedekind-Weber (1882) / Riemann-Roch for genus 0

deep.surprise_reason: The page gives a neat ideal-theoretic proof of Königsberger's irreducibility theorem, in the style of Hilbert's Zahlbericht period. The theorem itself and the ramification/norm argument are standard. The genus-0 class number remark is likewise elementary from a modern viewpoint. Interesting as a working note, but not novel.

checkable.asserts: Example with n=6, mu=2 (p=2), nu=3 (q=3): v2(a3)=2>=3/2, v2(a6)=3=nu; v3(a3)=1>=3/3, v3(a6)=2=mu. The theorem predicts irreducibility over Q.
x^6 - 2^3*3^2 is irreducible over Q (single slopes 1/2 at 2 and 1/3 at 3).
The degree-6 minimal polynomial x^6 - 72 confirms that n' = mu*nu = 6 for alpha = 2^(1/2)*3^(1/3).
Single slope 1/2 at p=2 but no coprime second prime. The theorem does not apply; check whether it factors, which illustrates that the hypothesis gcd(mu, nu) = 1 matters.

transcription_corrections: 'Setze j=(alpha, sqrt[mu]{p}) [?]' is most likely 'Setze j=(alpha, p)', i.e. the gcd ideal of alpha and p in Q(alpha).
'Ebenso folgt die Theilbarkeit durch mu' is mathematically required to be 'durch nu' (the manuscript may have nu, or it is Hilbert's slip).
'Separatabzuges' and 'Kronecker'schen Fundamentalgl.' are confirmed; 'Grundzüge' refers to Kronecker's Grundzüge einer arithmetischen Theorie der algebraischen Grössen.
